whatItDoes: Research a topic across the web, grade and revise the write-up against an editorial rubric, illustrate it, then build and deploy a live report site — not just a document. Reads the top sources in full, self-critiques the draft before it publishes, and can map the result onto a subdomain you own.
longDescription:
You give it a topic. It plans a couple of complementary search queries, gathers and dedupes candidate sources across them, reads the survivors for full text, and has an LLM write a structured, cited report — a title, a summary, and a handful of sections that reference where each claim came from.

Before anything gets built, a second model call grades that report against a fixed editorial bar — every section cites a source, no section just restates another, the tone fits the audience — and revises it if it falls short, bounded to a couple of attempts either way. It then generates an illustration or two, and hands the whole package to a coding agent that builds a self-contained static site, deploys it, and gives you back a URL you can send someone.

The self-critique and the illustrations are both boundable to zero cost: pass `maxDraftAttempts: 1` to skip the revise loop, or `illustrationCount: 0` to skip images. Neither failing gracefully — no sources, no picture, no revision — stops the run; each just narrows what gets built. The site build itself is a real coding-agent run that can take minutes: `build` launches it and pauses on its result, so the run costs nothing while the agent works, and wakes up at `publish` when the site is ready. `publish` re-attaches the sandbox the agent built in and deploys it to a stable preview URL. If you point a domain you own at it, `mapDomain` adds a free CNAME so the site answers at `report.your-domain.dev` instead; skip the domain and the preview URL is the deliverable.

Set `dryRun: true` and it stops once the report clears (or exhausts) self-critique, returning it without illustrating, building, deploying, or touching DNS — the free path `run_local` traces end to end before you spend anything.

You pay for the web searches, the scrapes, the two model calls per draft attempt (write, then grade), the illustrations, and the coding agent that builds the site — the pauses while jobs run, and the DNS record, are free. A dry run costs only the research and the self-critique.
notes:
Click **Use this template** — Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it. Your $5 signup credit covers first runs.

Give it a `topic` (what to research) and, optionally, an `audience` to tune the tone. `reviewThreshold` (default 0.7) and `maxDraftAttempts` (default 2) control the self-critique loop; `illustrationCount` (default 2, max 3) controls how many sections get a generated image — set it to 0 to skip illustration entirely. To publish under your own domain, register/own the domain in Sapiom first, then pass `customDomain` (a domain you own) and an optional `subdomain` (defaults to `www`) — it adds a free CNAME to the live site. Leave the domain off and you still get a shareable preview URL. Pass `dryRun: true` to get the report back — after self-critique — without illustrating, building, or deploying anything.

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` and `{ "topic": "...", "dryRun": true }` to trace plan → gather → synthesize → critique and read the report for free (capabilities stubbed, nothing built), or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.
